ogTitle: Top 10 Attractions in Nong Khai 2026 — Mekong Riverfront, Famous Temples, Naga, Skywalk
ogDesc: Sala Kaew Ku, Luang Pho Phra Sai, Naga Plaza by the Mekong, Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge, Wat Pha Tak Suea Skywalk, riverside markets — the best of Nong Khai in one list, with entrance fees, hours, and directions.
eyebrow: See it like a Nong Khai local · Updated 2026
intro: Nong Khai is a Mekong riverside city you can walk all day without getting bored — from the giant sculpture garden at Sala Kaew Ku to the glass-floor skywalk cantilevered over a cliff at Wat Pha Tak Suea. We've collected the 10 most talked-about attractions in one place: city-guardian temples, riverside markets, and the iconic naga photo spots — with entrance fees, hours, and directions all included. Plan your trip from this list alone.
chips: 🛕 City-guardian temples + Luang Pho Phra Sai

blocks.html:
Nong Khai's special quality is genuinely its riverside. Every evening, the whole city gravitates to the Mekong — a cool breeze, the sun dropping behind the Lao bank, then everyone dispersing to the markets for dinner. The old-city zone is walkable from end to end: Tha Sadet Market with its Indochina souvenirs, Naga Plaza in front of Wat Lam Duan, right through to Wat Pho Chai where Luang Pho Phra Sai is enshrined. Those looking for café-and-night-market vibes have Chic Chic Market with its colorful shipping containers, and Ban Mai Market where you can sit in a hay-bale chair and watch an outdoor cinema under the stars. For a full-scale view, drive north toward Sangkhom District and walk the glass-floor skywalk at Wat Pha Tak Suea — Mekong panoramas from a cliff edge.

Many places on this list are genuine provincial landmarks. Sala Kaew Ku is a sculpture park of over 200 concrete figures mixing Buddhist, Hindu, and Ramayana imagery, built over decades from the devotion of Pu Bun Lue Suri-rat — a place you won't find anywhere else. Wat Pho Chai is a royal monastery enshrining Luang Pho Phra Sai, a golden Buddha deeply venerated by Nong Khai and Lao communities on both sides of the river. Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge No. 1, over 1,170 meters long, is both the main border crossing into Laos and Nong Khai's most photographed structure. And Naga Plaza by the Mekong is the stage for the Ok Phansa festival and the legendary Naga Fireball phenomenon that draws crowds every year. One visit to Nong Khai covers art enthusiasts, devotees, photographers, and foodies alike — once you've walked the riverfront you'll understand why people keep coming back.

blocks.name: Sala Kaew Ku (Wat Khaek)
blocks.area: Hat Kham Sub-district, Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai
blocks.signature: Outdoor sculpture garden of over 200 giant concrete figures mixing Buddhist, Hindu, and Ramayana imagery — the large seven-headed naga is the star photo spot
blocks.descHtml:
Sala Kaew Ku — known locally as Wat Khaek — is one of Isan's most visually singular outdoor sculpture parks. Spread across 42 rai, the park contains over 200 reinforced concrete figures (around 208 in total), combining stories from Buddhism, Hinduism, the Ramayana, and local folk belief in one space. It was built from the devotion of Pu Bun Lue Suri-rat starting in 1978 under the idea that all religions can coexist. It is a natural fit for people who enjoy unusual art, spirit worship, photography, and families wanting to show children something that isn't an ordinary temple.

The unmissable highlight is the park's largest figure: a Buddha seated under a multi-headed naga canopy, about 25 meters tall — visible from a distance, and a photo spot where everyone stands beside it to capture the scale. Around the park are more than ten additional figures taller than a three-storey building — divine images, multi-headed nagas, and the Wheel of Life that you walk through, illustrating the cycle from birth to death. Multiple reviews note that the park initially feels a little uncanny, but once you're inside the sense of stillness and meaning takes over. The pavilion building also displays the preserved body of Pu Bun Lue for veneration.

Admission is wallet-friendly: Thai adults 20 THB, children 10 THB, foreigners 40 THB. Open daily 08:00–18:00. Walking through comfortably takes 1–2 hours. Located in Hat Kham Sub-district on the eastern bypass, only about 3–4 kilometers from downtown Nong Khai — under ten minutes by car — and close to the Friendship Bridge border crossing, so it works as a stop before or after crossing into Laos.

This park has held the top spot for Nong Khai tourism for a long time. Ratings are consistently high because there's genuinely nowhere else quite like it. One thing to know: the park is open-air and the midday sun is fierce. Come in the morning or late afternoon, wear a hat and bring water. Most signage is in Thai — if you bring foreign friends, plan to explain the stories yourself. The entrance area has a small food stall zone and a fish-feeding pond for children.
mustOrder: Naga-canopy Buddha — about 25 meters tall (the must-photograph spot)
Walk through the Wheel of Life and read the teachings
Giant divine and naga figures — over 200 in the park
Fish pond + entrance-area snacks
blocks.bestFor: Art and spirit worship lovers — come morning or late afternoon before crossing into Laos
blocks.zone: Eastern bypass, Hat Kham (near Friendship Bridge)

blocks.name: Tha Sadet Market (Mekong Riverside Walking Street)
blocks.area: Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai
blocks.signature: Covered riverside souvenir market — Indochina goods, food and household items from Laos, Vietnam, and China; Sat–Sun evening walking street
blocks.descHtml:
Tha Sadet Market — known locally as the Indochina Market — is the covered riverside souvenir market in the heart of the city that most Nong Khai visitors make their first stop. The defining feature is the almost-kilometer-long covered walkway that protects shoppers from both sun and rain. Inside it is densely packed with Indochina goods from Laos, Vietnam, and China — dried food, processed food, clothing, watches, souvenirs, kitchenware, and more. Anyone who enjoys a proper market stroll, hunting for gifts, and negotiating prices will feel at home here.

The unmissable move is walking the full length of the stalls on both sides, picking out souvenirs at prices lower than in Bangkok — and bargaining is expected and welcome. Vietnamese-style snacks like naem (fermented sausage) and moo yo are worth sampling. Once you exit toward the riverside, there's a walkway along the Mekong where you can look directly across the water to Laos and the Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge — a popular photo spot and beautiful sunset location. The Naga Plaza is close by for an extra check-in. The Saturday and Sunday evening walking street is especially lively — more stalls open, more people, and occasional live music.

Entry is free. Budget a few hundred baht for snacking and souvenirs and you're well set. The market is open daily, generally from around 09:00 to 18:00, with some stalls opening earlier and part of the market staying later into the evening. Located right on the Mekong riverfront within the city municipality — walkable from most central hotels, with parking near Naga Plaza.

One observation from real reviews: some visitors note the market has become quieter on weekdays in recent years, with some stalls closed. For the full lively atmosphere, Saturdays and Sundays are the call. Arrive before noon to avoid the worst of the midday heat. Google scores it around 4.2 from thousands of reviews — a Mekong riverside market well worth the stop for a first shop and first taste of Nong Khai.
mustOrder: Walk the Indochina stalls and negotiate for souvenirs
Sample Vietnamese-style naem and moo yo
Mekong riverbank view + Friendship Bridge + sunset
Sat–Sun Mekong Walking Street in the evening
blocks.bestFor: Souvenir shopping + Saturday and Sunday Mekong walking street in the evening

blocks.name: Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge No. 1
blocks.area: Mi Chai Sub-district, Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai
blocks.signature: Over 1,170-meter bridge crossing the Mekong linking Thailand and Laos — the main border crossing and a classic Mekong view photo spot
blocks.priceRange: Free (Thai-side viewing/photography) · official fees for actual border crossing
blocks.descHtml:
Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge No. 1 is the first bridge across the Mekong to link Nong Khai on the Thai side with Vientiane, the Lao capital. It stretches over 1,170 meters and has been in operation since 1994. It serves as both the main land border crossing for people entering Laos and as Nong Khai's most recognized landmark for river views. Come for the Mekong photo, for the atmosphere of a two-country border, or as the starting point for a trip to Vientiane.

The highlight most people mention is the wide, beautiful Mekong view from the water's edge — especially in the softer evening light. Walking along the park and garden on the Thai bank lets you look across at the bridge stretching toward the other side. Real reviewers say: "the Mekong view from the middle of the bridge is genuinely beautiful" — it's an easy, pleasant place to stroll and photograph. Some visitors enjoy watching vehicles and trains passing through — the bridge carries both road lanes and a railway track in a single combined structure.

The Thai-side viewing area and parkland are free, no admission. If you just want to photograph and walk along the Mekong, it costs nothing. Actually crossing into Laos requires clearing immigration, with documentation requirements and official border-crossing fees. Located in Mi Chai Sub-district on the eastern side of Nong Khai city — a short drive from the center, with parking at the border checkpoint.

This spot is popular because it is simultaneously a gateway to Laos and a symbol of Nong Khai in a single location. Everyone who visits the city typically comes here for a photo. One thing to know: the area around the checkpoint is busiest at midday — for good light and comfortable photography, evening is the recommendation. Restaurants near the checkpoint have mixed reviews for price and service; it may be better to eat further into town for more options.
mustOrder: Mekong river view from the bridge in the evening
Walk the riverside parkland on the Thai bank
Photograph the 1,170-meter bridge spanning the Mekong
Vientiane border gateway
blocks.bestFor: Mekong river photography + starting point for a Vientiane trip — evenings
blocks.zone: Mi Chai Sub-district (border crossing, eastern side of the city)
blocks.hours: Thai-side viewing accessible anytime · Border crossing open approx. 06:00–22:00

blocks.name: Wat Pho Chai (Luang Pho Phra Sai)
blocks.area: Nai Mueang Sub-district, Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai
blocks.signature: Royal monastery enshrining Luang Pho Phra Sai — the golden city-guardian Buddha, deeply venerated by Nong Khai and Lao communities
blocks.descHtml:
Wat Pho Chai is the royal monastery at the heart of Nong Khai city, enshrining "Luang Pho Phra Sai" — a Buddha image in the subduing-Mara posture cast in golden hue, the city-guardian figure revered by Nong Khai residents and the Lao community across the river for generations. If you're in Nong Khai and have time for only one temple, most people put this at the top. It suits merit-makers, those who love history and legend, and families bringing elders to pray. Google Maps rates it 4.7 from thousands of reviews — reflecting genuine popularity with both Thai and international visitors.

The unmissable experience is entering the ubosot to venerate Luang Pho Phra Sai in person. The figure is a radiant solid gold. The legend tells that it is one of three sibling Buddhas — Phra Suk, Phra Soem, and Phra Sai — created by a daughter of a Lan Xang king. When being transported across the Mekong, Phra Suk sank mid-river. When Phra Sai was later being brought to Bangkok, the cart carrying it broke down at this exact temple — taken as an omen that the image should remain in Nong Khai. Also unmissable: the mural paintings wrapping the ubosot walls, telling the story of the image's legend and the life of the Buddha — vivid and detailed, rewarding a slow walk around.

The temple grounds are shaded, spacious, with large trees and shade canopies. Multiple real reviews say the temple is well-organized and not crowded inside the sacred zone because the parking lot, market area, and food stalls are all arranged in the outer zone. Entry is free — just a merit donation box. Light incense and candles at the pavilion outside; no incense inside the ubosot. Remove shoes before entering.

Located on Prachak Road, Nai Mueang Sub-district — central and easy to reach. Open daily roughly 06:00–19:00. The busiest period is Songkran, when there is a ceremonial procession to enthrone Luang Pho Phra Sai on a royal chariot and lead it around the city for the public to pour ceremonial water. For quiet and a genuinely serene visit, come in the morning before crowds arrive.
mustOrder: Venerate Luang Pho Phra Sai — the golden Buddha in the ubosot
Walk the mural paintings telling the legend of the image
Make merit — fortune-telling sticks (sian si) by request
Ceremonial bathing procession during Songkran
blocks.bestFor: Devotional visits and family merit-making — morning is best

blocks.name: Naga Plaza by the Mekong (Cultural Plaza in front of Wat Lam Duan)
blocks.signature: Two large naga figures about 15 meters tall spraying water on the Mekong bank — venue for the Ok Phansa festival and the Naga Fireball phenomenon
blocks.descHtml:
Naga Plaza — known to Nong Khai residents as the Cultural Plaza in front of Wat Lam Duan — is a public open-air space on the Mekong riverfront in the center of the city, directly adjacent to Tha Sadet Market. The focal point is a pair of large nagas, each about 15 meters tall with bodies roughly 45 meters long, spraying water from their mouths and facing the river. Anyone passing through Nong Khai who wants an iconic photo of the city's landmark should stop here. It suits families, couples, and anyone who enjoys a leisurely riverside walk.

The most beautiful time is in the evening into early night — the sun softens, a cool river breeze comes off the Mekong, and reviewers consistently agree: come when the naga fountain is running and the lights are on; the colors are far more impressive than midday. One single shot gets you nagas, river, and sunset in the same frame. Around the plaza the riverside walkway stretches for a long stretch where locals exercise, run, cycle, and bring children to play every evening — a genuinely local, lived-in feel.

Free, public space, open 24 hours. Parking is available along the road. Once you've walked the plaza, continue directly into Tha Sadet Market next door. Plenty of riverside food options surround the area: Vietnamese-style naem nuang, Isan food, Mekong river fish, and moo kata (Thai barbecue hot pot) — pay only for what you eat. A budget riverside evening is very possible.

This plaza is well known as both a city check-in landmark and the venue for large events — particularly Ok Phansa, when Nong Khai holds its big riverside festival and the Naga Fireball phenomenon is viewed from here in the late evenings of the 15th night of the 11th lunar month, drawing huge crowds. One thing to know: don't confuse this with Sala Kaew Ku (Wat Khaek), which is the sculpture park — a different place several kilometers away. Midday sun is strong on this open riverside strip — an umbrella or hat helps.
mustOrder: Photograph the two large naga water-spraying figures — about 15 meters tall — when the fountain runs at dusk
Watch the evening lights over the Mekong
Continue into Tha Sadet Market directly next door
Come during Ok Phansa / Naga Fireball season if timing allows
blocks.bestFor: Riverside landmark photography in the evening
blocks.hours: Open 24 hrs daily (fountain / lights active in the evening)
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Naga Plaza by the Mekong, Nong Khai · Christophe95 · Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 4.0

blocks.title: 🛏️ Hotels in Nong Khai — riverside or city center
blocks.text: Staying overnight in Nong Khai makes the trip far more relaxed. A riverside hotel means waking up to Mekong views and being able to walk to Tha Sadet Market and Naga Plaza in minutes. A central hotel near Asawann is convenient in every direction. Options range from budget riverside guesthouses to mid-range hotels. Compare prices across booking sites and book ahead — especially during the Ok Phansa and Naga Fireball festival period when rooms fill quickly.

blocks.name: Chic Chic Market
blocks.area: Nong Kom Kao, Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai
blocks.signature: Colorful shipping-container night market — charcoal hot pot, bars, live music, a real aircraft as a landmark, open 15:00 to midnight
blocks.descHtml:
If you want a chilled-out evening in Nong Khai with somewhere to wander, photograph, and eat, Chic Chic Market is where city residents gather after dark. The signature look is multi-colored shipping containers arranged as shop rows — yellow, red, and blue containers line the road from the entrance, plus a real aircraft parked as a landmark that kids find immediately exciting. It works for families, groups of friends, and couples wanting a spot to sit and enjoy the evening breeze.

The must-try is the charcoal claypot — a small earthen pot over charcoal, homey and satisfying, consistently praised in real reviews. Drinkers have bars like Runway Bar and Flow Bar, and the most talked-about spot is the rooftop deck near the aircraft wings — a unique photo angle. The market has scattered small restaurant stalls in different styles to browse and graze through, an Amazon Café, a kids' zone, and regular live music at night.

No admission fee — just pay for food and drinks. Budget per head is local market pricing. Located on the bypass road along Mittraphap Road near the shopping mall, easy to drive to, with a large parking lot accommodating well over a hundred vehicles plus motorbike parking. Open 15:00–00:00 daily. Coming around sunset gets you both golden-hour light and the lit-up night atmosphere.

Locals appreciate it because it combines eating, drinking, walking, and photo spots in one place without requiring formal attire. Google scores it around 4.2 from several hundred reviews. One thing to know: evenings and weekends get crowded — arrive slightly early for a good seat in a prime section. Part of the market has roofed areas that provide some rain cover.
mustOrder: Charcoal claypot hot pot
Rooftop deck near the aircraft wing
Colorful container photo wall + real aircraft
Runway/Flow Bar and live music
blocks.bestFor: Evening meal with family or friends

blocks.name: Ban Mai Market (Nong Khai)
blocks.area: Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai
blocks.signature: Evening market with a wooden-village atmosphere — outdoor cinema zone, hay-bale chairs, live music, wide range of food stalls
blocks.priceRange: Free entry · food from tens to low hundreds of THB
blocks.descHtml:
Ban Mai Market is an evening market in the center of Nong Khai that you come to not just for shopping — you come to sit long and eat and drink at a leisurely pace from late afternoon until dark. Suited for anyone wanting a relaxed spot after a full day on the riverfront, whether with a group of friends, family, or a couple who wants to sit quietly with music in the background. The defining feature is the wooden-village style decor that gives the whole place a warm, unhurried feeling, with a shopping zone, a drinks zone, and food restaurants spread throughout. Nong Khai locals come here regularly — this isn't a market built purely for tourists.

The highlight that multiple reviews consistently mention is the "outdoor cinema zone" with seats made from hay bales — sit down and you get a genuinely Isan countryside feeling, layered with soft live music. Food options are wide: a large moo kata (Thai barbecue hot pot) restaurant, seafood, jum jim (Isan hot pot), pla jum (fish hot pot — reviews praise the large, firm fish), through to affordable steak restaurants and the hip Isan café zap cafe with creatively named drinks. Laab and som tam fans have several local Isan choices.

No entry fee — market prices throughout. Decent parking in front. Located on Mittraphap Road in Nong Kom Kao Sub-district, about 3 kilometers from the Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge. Easily reached from the city center or from the border side. Open from around 16:00 until roughly 22:00 daily.

People like it because it combines food, music, and atmosphere in one easy-access place without needing to dress up. One thing to know: evenings get busier, especially Fridays and Saturdays — if you're coming in a larger group and want the hay-bale cinema section or a table near the stage, arrive a little earlier for a prime spot. Bring some cash since not all stalls take mobile transfers.
mustOrder: Outdoor cinema zone with hay-bale chairs
Pla jum (fish hot pot) / seafood
Large moo kata (Thai barbecue hot pot)
Evening live music
blocks.bestFor: A relaxed evening sitting long with friends or family

blocks.name: Asawann Shopping Complex (Big Chiang)
blocks.signature: The central mall of Nong Khai — shops, supermarket, cinema, food, all under one roof
blocks.descHtml:
If you want a single-stop destination in Nong Khai for shopping, eating, and picking up gifts to take home, Asawann Shopping Complex 1 — known to locals as "Big Chiang" — is the answer. This large mall in the center of the city on Mittraphap Road has been here long enough to become a meeting point for Nong Khai residents. Walk in and you find Lotus's (formerly Tesco Lotus) as the main supermarket, Power Buy for electronics, TG Phone for mobile, several bank branches, a food court, restaurants, and a Major Cineplex cinema — all in one building. A natural stop for anyone who wants to escape the Isan heat, sit in cool air over a meal, and stroll comfortably.

The highlight that visitors particularly mention is the food court — foreigner-friendly, with an English menu, making it easy to order without guessing. The stalls cover local Isan food, rice-and-curry, noodle dishes, sushi, and desserts. Prices are typical of a provincial-town mall — meaning not expensive, mostly in the tens to low hundreds of THB per dish. Another must: walk around Lotus's to pick up food gifts — because the mall is close to Tha Sadet Market and the Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge, both Thai and Lao shoppers use it regularly, especially on weekends when the atmosphere is especially lively.

Very convenient location: 311 Moo 10, Mittraphap Road, Mi Chai Sub-district, central Nong Khai. Open daily 10:00–21:00. Free parking on the ground-floor lot and in the parking structure. Google rates it 4.1 from hundreds of reviews — general agreement that it is a complete and comfortable one-stop destination. The note that comes up consistently in reviews: peak times and long weekends see the parking lot fill up — coming on a weekday morning or early afternoon gives a more relaxed experience. Worth a stop on any Nong Khai trip before heading to the riverside or Friendship Bridge.
mustOrder: Food court — English menu available
Lotus's supermarket for food gifts
Major Cineplex cinema
Local Isan food in the food court
blocks.bestFor: A meal, household shopping, and a cool mid-trip break in Nong Khai

blocks.name: Lan Bueng Wiang (Mekong Riverfront Plaza — Seven-Headed Naga)
blocks.area: Si Chiang Mai District, Nong Khai
blocks.signature: A shaded riverside plaza with a towering golden seven-headed naga — photo spot with views of the Mekong and Vientiane directly across the water
blocks.descHtml:
Lan Bueng Wiang is the cultural riverside plaza that has become the landmark of Si Chiang Mai District in Nong Khai. The star here is "Phaya Sri Suwan Hong Sattha-nakharat" — a golden seven-headed naga standing tall with its body facing the Mekong. The name Bueng Wiang is Isan for "looking toward Vientiane" — because this plaza faces directly across from the Lao capital. Standing at the railing you can see the Lao bank clearly. Visitors who want a wide, atmospheric Mekong view, inexpensive photography, and a family space with room for children to run around will find this spot worthwhile.

The must-photograph is the seven-headed naga figure with the Mekong and Vientiane as the backdrop. Evening light is beautiful here — reviewers consistently agree that coming in the late afternoon is the best call: cool river breeze, soft light, and a long comfortable walk. If you visit on a Saturday evening, there's a riverside walking street nearby with food and souvenirs. Tuesday mornings see local community members in traditional dress offering alms — a genuinely local experience.

Free public space, open 24 hours, no entry fee. Budget is just whatever you spend on the small food stalls along the plaza edge. Parking available. Located on the riverside in Phan Phrao Sub-district, Si Chiang Mai — reachable from Nong Khai city without too much difficulty. People like this spot because it combines a beautiful Mekong view, a striking naga check-in, and the Mekong cultural belief all in the same place.

One thing to know: the plaza is open and exposed — the midday sun is fierce. Bring an umbrella or hat, and plan your visit for the evening. If you're targeting the full experience, aim for a Saturday or for the Ok Phansa festival season when Si Chiang Mai holds its own Naga Fireball event.
mustOrder: Photograph Phaya Sri Suwan Hong Sattha-nakharat — the golden seven-headed naga
Watch sunset and look across to Vientiane on the opposite bank
Riverside walking street (Saturday evenings)
Stand by the Mekong railing and enjoy the breeze
blocks.bestFor: Sunset Mekong views + seven-headed naga check-in
blocks.hours: Open daily 24 hrs (public plaza) · Walking street Sat evenings
blocks.libCredit: Illustration: Street food · Charles Haynes / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 2.0)

blocks.name: Wat Pha Tak Suea (Skywalk)
blocks.signature: Glass-floor skywalk cantilevered over a cliff — panoramic view of the curving Mekong and the Lao bank
blocks.descHtml:
Wat Pha Tak Suea sits on a ridge above the Mekong River in Sangkhom District, well north of downtown Nong Khai. The temple is known because of its "skywalk" — a glass-floor platform cantilevered out over the cliff edge, widely considered one of Thailand's first of its kind. Anyone who wants a wide view, merit-making at a beautiful temple, and an outstanding photograph will find this spot worth the drive. Climb to the summit terrace and you'll find a large Buddha image, naga sculptures, and a viewing balcony looking directly down over the curving Mekong and the Lao bank in full panorama.

The unmissable experience is stepping onto the glass floor at the cliff's edge — look straight down through the transparent surface and feel the height in your stomach, then look out over the sweeping Mekong bend below. The view many visitors find more memorable than the glass itself is the wide Mekong panorama stretching to the horizon. Winter mornings sometimes bring a sea of mist floating above the river — like standing above clouds. Google users rate it around 4.4 stars. Most praise the view as genuinely beautiful; some note the actual glass section is shorter than expected, but the Mekong view compensates fully.

Entry to the temple is free. The skywalk has no separate admission, but shoe covers are required before stepping on the glass — 20 THB per pair at the service point. The whole trip costs almost nothing. Temple open daily roughly 06:00–18:00; skywalk zone typically opens 08:00–17:00. The approach road is steep and winding — check your brakes and drive carefully. The spot is popular as a check-in on the riverside highway through Sangkhom District, and photos come out well from every angle.

Key things to know before you go: the mountain road gets challenging for larger vehicles in places. On holidays you may queue to step onto the glass and get only a short time on it. Going early avoids both the midday heat and the crowd. Wear socks or bring them for the shoe-cover service. Dress modestly — it's an active temple. The glass can feel unsteady when others are walking nearby, but it is structurally sound.
mustOrder: Walk the glass-floor skywalk cantilevered over the cliff
Panoramic view of the curving Mekong + Lao bank
Sea of mist on winter mornings
Large Buddha and naga sculptures at the summit
blocks.bestFor: Morning sea of mist + Mekong panorama — photographers and hikers
blocks.zone: Sangkhom District (north of the city along the Mekong)

blocks.title: 🎟️ Book tickets and tours in Nong Khai — skip the queue
blocks.text: Nong Khai covers many spots in a single day. If you'd rather not drive yourself or worry about finding the road up to Wat Pha Tak Suea, booking a guided tour with a driver through Klook or GetYourGuide saves time. Some packages cover several riverside attractions in one route — Sala Kaew Ku, major temples, and viewpoints — with a single combined ticket. Book ahead so you can focus on the experience rather than logistics.

blocks.title: Know before you go — Nong Khai

items.title: Getting around
items.text: Grab is scarce in Nong Khai and wait times are long. The old-city area is walkable, but out-of-city spots like Wat Pha Tak Suea (Sangkhom District) and Sala Kaew Ku are best reached by private car or motorbike rental. That's the most flexible option.

items.title: Bring cash
items.text: Riverside markets, street food stalls, Sala Kaew Ku admission, and the Skywalk shoe covers are all cash only. Keep small bills in the 20–100 THB range. Shops inside Asawann mall accept card and QR payment.

items.title: Beat the queue and the sun
items.text: Going up to Wat Pha Tak Suea's skywalk early morning gives the clearest sky and fewest people. The Mekong Walking Street is liveliest on Saturday and Sunday evenings — arriving before 17:00 makes finding parking and seating much easier.

items.title: Dress for temples
items.text: Wat Pho Chai and Wat Pha Tak Suea are sacred sites. Cover shoulders and knees, remove shoes before entering the viharn, and speak quietly when others are praying.

items.title: Language
items.text: Most signage and menus are in Thai. Sala Kaew Ku and the Friendship Bridge have some English. A Google Translate camera is useful for reading market menus. Nong Khai locals are friendly and helpful.

items.title: Crossing to Laos
items.text: Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge No. 1 is the main border crossing. If you plan to cross to Vientiane, bring a valid passport and complete the official immigration process on both sides. Thai-side river viewing and photography is free.

blocks.title: How to plan 1–2 days in Nong Khai
blocks.html:
The simplest approach is dividing into "city" and "outside the city." Day one is easy in the old city. Start the morning at Wat Pho Chai to venerate Luang Pho Phra Sai, then stop at Sala Kaew Ku on the bypass near the Friendship Bridge (open 08:00–18:00, Thais 20 THB). Continue to Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge No. 1 for the Mekong photo. In the evening, walk to Tha Sadet Market and then Naga Plaza by the Mekong in front of Wat Lam Duan — right next door — to watch the naga fountain when the lights come on. Close the night at Chic Chic Market (open from 15:00 to midnight) or Ban Mai Market with its outdoor cinema.

If you have a second day, drive north to Sangkhom District to walk the glass-floor skywalk at Wat Pha Tak Suea (free entry, shoe cover 20 THB). The mountain road warrants going in clear daylight. On the way, stop at Lan Bueng Wiang in Si Chiang Mai to photograph the seven-headed naga with Vientiane in the background. For take-home gifts — naem sausage, fermented pork sausage, Isan dried goods — buy at Tha Sadet Market or stop at Asawann Shopping Complex (Big Chiang) in the city center before heading out.

blocks.text: Staying overnight in Nong Khai makes a big difference — wake early, walk the riverfront in the morning cool, visit the temples before the crowds, then drive up to Sangkhom for the Skywalk in clear daylight. Riverside and city-center hotels are available at every budget. Check prices and book ahead.

faq.q: ❓ First time in Nong Khai — what can't I miss?
faq.a: Three places that define Nong Khai are Sala Kaew Ku — a sculpture garden of over 200 giant concrete figures found nowhere else — · Wat Pho Chai, the royal monastery enshrining Luang Pho Phra Sai, the city guardian Buddha — · and the old-city Mekong riverfront, where Tha Sadet Market and Naga Plaza in front of Wat Lam Duan are right next to each other for a full evening walk. If you have more time, continue to the glass-floor Skywalk at Wat Pha Tak Suea in Sangkhom District.

faq.q: ❓ What are the top photography spots in Nong Khai?
faq.a: The most popular photo spots are: the seven-headed naga at Sala Kaew Ku · the glass-floor Skywalk at Wat Pha Tak Suea cantilevered over the cliff with a panoramic Mekong bend below · Naga Plaza by the Mekong in front of Wat Lam Duan with its water-spraying twin nagas · and Lan Bueng Wiang in Si Chiang Mai where you can photograph the seven-headed naga with Vientiane directly across the water in the same frame.

faq.q: ❓ What are the entrance fees for Nong Khai attractions?
faq.a: Most sites are free or very low cost. · Sala Kaew Ku: Thai adults 20 THB, children 10 THB, foreigners 40 THB. · Wat Pha Tak Suea: temple entry free; shoe covers for the Skywalk 20 THB. · Wat Pho Chai, Tha Sadet Market, Naga Plaza by the Mekong, Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge (Thai side), Lan Bueng Wiang, and the various night markets are all free — pay only for food and things you buy.

faq.q: ❓ Should I drive myself, and is parking easy?
faq.a: Attractions are spread across the province, so having your own transport is the most flexible option. The old-city area is walkable, but Sala Kaew Ku, the Friendship Bridge, and especially Wat Pha Tak Suea in Sangkhom District (which follows the riverside highway north of town) are all outside the city center. A private car or rental gives the most freedom. · Night markets like Chic Chic Market have large parking lots handling hundreds of vehicles. The road up to Wat Pha Tak Suea is a mountain road — check your vehicle and go in the daytime.

faq.q: ❓ What are the opening hours for Nong Khai attractions?
faq.a: Sala Kaew Ku and Wat Pha Tak Suea open roughly 08:00–18:00 and 06:00–18:00 respectively — daytime visits. · Tha Sadet Market is open daily roughly midday to evening; the riverside walking street is busiest Saturday and Sunday evenings. · Chic Chic Market opens from 15:00 to midnight daily, and Ban Mai Market is an evening market from mid-afternoon to late night. · Temples, Naga Plaza, and the Thai-side Friendship Bridge viewing area are accessible throughout the day.
